To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the CRF approach with word based labelling and widow size is more effective for SBD in the Thai language, and (2) the BiLSTM-CRF approach is not suitable for SBD in Thai.
the CRF model outperformed BiLSTM CRFs on Thai sentence boundary detection.
CRF outperformed BiLSTM-CRF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a Thai SBD model that can be used in the development of a sentiment analysis and machine translation system for Thai.
the development of a Thai SBD model that can be used in the real world.
a comparison of two SBD models, which can be applied to a Thai corpus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CRF approach is the best approach for the SBD task in the Thai language.
the CRF is a better model for SBD than the BiLSTM-CRF.
the BiLSTM-CRF model with the window size of 5 words performed the best in the Thai language, with an F1 score of 0.93.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CRF model with a window size of 2 is the most suitable for Thai SBD.
the CRF model is a better approach to the SBD task for Thai language, when compared with the BiLSTM model.
the word based labellling approach with the widow size of 3 outperformed other approaches in the SBD task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple word based CRF can be applied to a real world textual dataset.
the CRF approach is more suitable for SBD in Thai than the BiLSTM approach.
the CRF approach is more effective for the task of Thai SBD.
